## Excursions around Mexico City's Zócalo: comparing itineraries

[Mexico City's Zócalo](/mexico/place/mexico-city-zocalo/), also called Constitution Square, is in the capital's historic center. It is surrounded by the [Metropolitan Cathedral](/mexico/place/mexico-city-metropolitan-cathedral/) and [National Palace](/mexico/place/national-palace-mexico-city/), with the ruins of the [Templo Mayor](/mexico/place/templo-mayor/) nearby. On a single walk, you can compare ancient Tenochtitlan with the Spanish colonial city.

The Zócalo is a starting point for several excursions. Some continue to parks and museums, while others focus on religious history. To choose, compare the subsequent stops, duration and included services, not just the square itself.

## Which excursions pass through the Zócalo?

**[Eternal Streets and Cultural Treasures](/mexico/mexico-city-and-teotihuacan/mexico-city-history-anthropology-tour/)** is a **6-hour** excursion. It combines the Zócalo, the cathedral, Templo Mayor and historic streets, followed by the [National Museum of Anthropology](/mexico/place/national-museum-of-anthropology/). Shared transportation, a certified bilingual guide and museum entry are included. The guiding languages are English and Spanish. Meals, drinks, tips and personal expenses are excluded.

**[Mexico City: Zócalo, Chapultepec and the Anthropology Museum](/mexico/mexico-city-and-teotihuacan/mexico-city-zocalo-chapultepec-anthropology/)** runs from the historic center to [Chapultepec](/mexico/place/chapultepec/) and the museum. It includes the cathedral, Templo Mayor and a possible visit to the National Palace when access is permitted. An English-speaking guide accompanies the excursion, and tickets are included in the selected program. Its duration should be confirmed separately.

**[Mexico City Churches, Mass and Garibaldi Square](/mexico/santo-domingo-mexico-city/mexico-city-pilgrimage-garibaldi/)** is a private itinerary with an English-speaking guide. After the Zócalo, travelers attend Mass at Santo Domingo, visit the Metropolitan Cathedral and other downtown buildings, then continue to Garibaldi Square with mariachi music. Private transportation and one Mass are included.

| Program | Distinguishing feature |
|---|---|
| Eternal Streets | 6 hours, historic center and museum |
| Zócalo and Chapultepec | Center, park and anthropology |
| Churches and Garibaldi | Private tour and Mass |

Shared attractions do not make the excursions identical. The six-hour duration and included museum ticket of the first program, in particular, do not imply the same terms for the other two.

## Why the Zócalo matters

Mexico City's historic center and Xochimilco are on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The ancient city of Tenochtitlan occupied the site of the present capital, with colonial buildings subsequently developed around its old center.

The [Metropolitan Cathedral](/mexico/place/mexico-city-metropolitan-cathedral/) stands on the square's north side, the [Templo Mayor](/mexico/place/templo-mayor/) survives nearby, and the [National Palace](/mexico/place/national-palace-mexico-city/) occupies the east side. A walking tour offers the chance to explore these landmarks together rather than treating them as attractions in different districts.

Travelers wishing to devote more time to the cathedral can explore [excursions that include it](/mexico/mexico-city-metropolitan-cathedral/). Archaeology and culture enthusiasts may prefer an itinerary pairing the Zócalo with the Anthropology Museum and Templo Mayor.

## What to consider when choosing

For an introduction, the **6-hour program** is convenient when a known duration and a mix of city sights and museum exhibits matter. The other sightseeing itinerary includes Chapultepec but requires separate agreement on timing. The private pilgrimage suits travelers interested in churches, Mass and religious history.

The Zócalo hosts major public events. Access to certain buildings, particularly the National Palace, may be restricted during official occasions. **A site being listed does not necessarily guarantee entry to its interior.**

Wear comfortable shoes and bring sun protection for walking. If needed, arrange a suitable pace and brief rest stops in advance.

## Frequently asked questions about Zócalo excursions

### Are the Zócalo and Metropolitan Cathedral the same place?

No. The [Zócalo](/mexico/place/mexico-city-zocalo/) is a city square, while the [Metropolitan Cathedral](/mexico/place/mexico-city-metropolitan-cathedral/) stands on its northern side. Tours often include both.

### Which excursion lasts 6 hours?

The [Eternal Streets and Cultural Treasures tour](/mexico/mexico-city-and-teotihuacan/mexico-city-history-anthropology-tour/) specifies **6 hours**. The durations of the other two should be checked separately.

### Can the Zócalo be combined with the Anthropology Museum?

Yes. Two city tours include the [National Museum of Anthropology](/mexico/place/national-museum-of-anthropology/). Their included services and order of stops differ.

### Can you always enter the National Palace?

No. The published pilgrimage itinerary notes that entry can be restricted during official events. Plans should account for this possibility.

## Excursions to Mitla from Oaxaca: itinerary and highlights

[Mitla](/mexico/place/mitla/) lies in the Tlacolula Valley east of [Oaxaca](/mexico/place/oaxaca/). It is an ancient Zapotec center famous for geometric patterns made from precisely fitted stones. Here the walls and inner courtyards reward close attention, while [Monte Albán](/mexico/place/monte-alban/) draws visitors with broad plazas, platforms and valley views.

A visit to Mitla may focus solely on the archaeological site or combine it with regional crafts and natural attractions. The current Ada Tours excursion takes the latter approach.

## How the 9–10-hour excursion works

The [Mitla, Weaving Traditions, Natural Wonders and Mezcal excursion](/mexico/mitla/mitla-hierve-el-agua-mescal-tour/) lasts **9–10 hours**. Morning pickup takes place approximately **between 9:00 and 9:30**, with shared transportation and guiding in English or Spanish.

The program combines four experiences:

- **[Mitla](/mexico/place/mitla/)** — ancient palace structures and geometric stone mosaics.
- **[Teotitlán del Valle](/mexico/place/teotitlan-del-valle/)** — traditional weaving workshops, natural dyes and handicrafts.
- **[Hierve el Agua](/mexico/place/hierve-el-agua/)** — mineral formations resembling petrified waterfalls and valley panoramas.
- **Mezcal production** — an explanation of how the agave spirit is made, followed by a tasting.

Each place reveals a different aspect of the region. It is a busy day, with time shared among transfers, archaeology, craft workshops and natural attractions.

## What is included in the price?

Included are **shared transportation, a certified bilingual guide, entrance to the archaeological site and Hierve el Agua, and a mezcal tasting**. Meals, tips and personal expenses are excluded.

No separate price for the excursion is stated in this collection. It cannot be inferred from the cost of a multi-day trip; nor should one assume the stand-alone excursion includes private transportation, as the published offer specifies shared transfers.

## What makes the Mitla archaeological site distinctive?

According to Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH), Mitla's monuments form several architectural groups. Its most striking feature is intricate stone mosaic decoration on the inside and outside walls. The patterns consist of individually worked pieces and demonstrate Zapotec craftsmanship.

A guided excursion helps explain the development of the ancient center and the decoration of its different spaces. If you prefer to examine the details independently and at length, bear in mind the pace of a four-stop excursion: the ruins occupy only part of the day.

## Mitla or Monte Albán?

| Site | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| [Mitla](/mexico/place/mitla/) | Mosaics, halls and inner courtyards |
| [Monte Albán](/mexico/place/monte-alban/) | Monumental plazas and views |

Both sites are linked to the region's ancient heritage, but **Monte Albán is not a stop** on the listed Mitla excursion. Seeing both requires a separately planned visit. To compare larger routes, explore [Mexico tours](/mexico/tour/) or [cultural and historical journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Preparing for the trip

Bring comfortable shoes for stone paths and natural terraces, sun protection and water. Check in advance how much time is allowed at the archaeological site and natural attraction, especially if traveling with limited mobility or children.

At [Hierve el Agua](/mexico/place/hierve-el-agua/), access to specific areas and the water depends on site regulations. Swimming should not be taken as a guaranteed part of the itinerary. The mezcal tasting is included, but individual participation can be discussed separately without assuming any change in price.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions to Mitla

### How long is a trip through Mitla and Hierve el Agua?

The [Ada Tours excursion](/mexico/mitla/mitla-hierve-el-agua-mescal-tour/) is listed as **9–10 hours**, including the weaving village and mezcal producer.

### Is entry to Mitla included?

Yes. Admission to the archaeological site is among the included services. Meals, tips and personal expenses are paid separately.

### Are Mitla and Monte Albán part of the same program?

No. [Monte Albán](/mexico/place/monte-alban/) is not on this itinerary. You need a different visit or additional time.

### Can I book a trip to Mitla only?

Our excursion includes several stops. Any itinerary changes must be discussed individually; the published listing does not confirm a ready-made Mitla-only product.

## Mitla, Hierve el Agua, weaving and mezcal: a 9–10-hour excursion

The surroundings of [Oaxaca](/mexico/place/oaxaca/) combine archaeology, crafts and unusual natural formations. One activity-filled day lets you admire the geometric stone patterns of ancient Mitla, discover textile production at Teotitlán del Valle, see Hierve el Agua's mineral cascades and learn how mezcal is made.

The Ada Tours excursion lasts **approximately 9–10 hours**, with pickup scheduled **between 9:00 and 9:30 a.m.** and guiding in **English and Spanish**. It includes shared transportation, a certified bilingual guide, entrance tickets to the archaeological site and Hierve el Agua, plus a mezcal tasting. **Meals, tips and personal expenses are not included.**

## Mitla: stone geometry and Zapotec heritage

[Mitla](/mexico/place/mitla/) is an important archaeological site in the Tlacolula Valley. Rather than enormous pyramids, its attractions are halls and walls decorated with delicate stone mosaics. Geometric patterns form friezes made of repeating elements, displaying the skill of ancient builders.

Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) links Mitla's distinctive decoration with Zapotec architectural traditions. Several groups of buildings survive, and their designs offer insight into the region's public and ceremonial life.

The excursion introduces the history of the site but does not allow free access to all restricted architectural areas. Visitors must follow site rules and avoid touching ancient decoration where forbidden.

## Teotitlán del Valle: how textiles are made

The next stop is [Teotitlán del Valle](/mexico/place/teotitlan-del-valle/), a settlement known for its weaving workshops. You meet local artisans who demonstrate the preparation of threads, natural dyes and the operation of looms.

The visit reveals how much work goes into the patterns on a rug or fabric. Colors come from plants and other natural materials, and geometric designs emerge as threads are woven. The production demonstration is engaging even for visitors with little previous interest in handicrafts.

Buying items is a personal choice; **souvenirs are not included** in the listed services. Seek permission before photographing people or their workspaces.

## Hierve el Agua: why the waterfalls look petrified

[Hierve el Agua](/mexico/place/hierve-el-agua/) is known for two large mineral formations resembling frozen waterfalls. They were formed by deposits left by spring water as it emerged at the surface. Over time, pale cascades accumulated down the slopes toward a deep ravine.

These are **not streams that froze in an instant**, but geological formations that developed gradually. Oaxaca's official tourism portal describes natural pools and viewpoints here. The trip offers views of distinctive rock textures and mountain scenery.

You can enjoy the panoramas and approach the natural pools. Actual access to the water, swimming arrangements and restrictions depend on conditions at the site on the day. Stay within safety barriers and away from cliff edges while taking photos.

## Mezcal: tasting and traditional production

The final part of the excursion focuses on Oaxacan **mezcal**, a spirit made from agave. At a traditional distillery, visitors learn about the stages of production and may sample the drink. **The tasting is included in the excursion price.**

Oaxaca is famous for diverse agave varieties and regional mezcal-making methods. It is particularly interesting to learn how the raw material and processing affect the flavor. The exact number and selection of samples are not specified for this excursion, so particular brands or a number of tastings are not promised.

The tasting is voluntary and intended for adults under applicable regulations. Travelers who do not drink alcohol should discuss an alternative way of learning about production in advance.

## What the excursion day price includes

The current Ada Tours service list confirms shared transportation, a certified bilingual guide, admission to Mitla and Hierve el Agua, and a mezcal tasting. **Meals, tips and personal purchases are excluded.** Do not assume additional private services based on similarities with another operator's excursions.

| Included | Paid separately |
|---|---|
| Shared transportation | Meals |
| English-/Spanish-speaking guide | Tips |
| Main admission tickets | Personal purchases |
| Mezcal tasting | Unspecified extras |

This is a long excursion, so bring water and a light snack, as meals are at your expense. Comfortable shoes, a hat and sun protection help with walks at Mitla and Hierve el Agua. Adjust the walking pace to the group's abilities on uneven ground and in strong heat.

Compare other cultural excursions on the [Mitla page](/mexico/mitla/) and in the [Culture and History collection](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about Mitla, Hierve el Agua and mezcal

### How long does the excursion last?

Approximately 9–10 hours; the published pickup time is around 9:00–9:30 a.m.

### Are admission tickets included?

Yes, the listed services include tickets to the archaeological site and Hierve el Agua.

### Will there be a mezcal tasting?

Yes, it is among the included services. The exact samples and tasting arrangements depend on the chosen venue.

### Can we swim at Hierve el Agua?

The itinerary mentions natural pools, but whether swimming is permitted depends on the site's rules and conditions. It cannot be guaranteed without checking.

### Are meals included?

No. Meals, tips and personal expenses are specified as exclusions.

## Tours including the excursion to Mitla, Hierve el Agua and mezcal production

The [Mitla, Weaving Traditions, Natural Wonders and Mezcal excursion](/mexico/mitla/mitla-hierve-el-agua-mescal-tour/) combines four distinct experiences in the Oaxaca region: Zapotec architecture in [Mitla](/mexico/place/mitla/), textile workshops in [Teotitlán del Valle](/mexico/place/teotitlan-del-valle/), mineral cascades at [Hierve el Agua](/mexico/place/hierve-el-agua/) and an introduction to mezcal production. It lasts **9–10 hours**.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} visiting Mitla and Hierve el Agua. The excursion is part of the [12-day Viva Mexico program](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/) and takes place **on day 8**, when travelers are already in [Oaxaca](/mexico/place/oaxaca/).

## How the excursion fits into Viva Mexico

On the [Viva Mexico tour](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/), discovery of the region begins after the Mexico City segment. **Day 6** is devoted to Oaxaca city and additional cultural activities; **day 7** explores Monte Albán and traditional crafts in nearby settlements. **Day 8** moves on to Mitla, weaving workshops, mineral springs and mezcal.

The geography then changes: **day 9** takes travelers from Oaxaca to Mérida, with subsequent days across the Yucatán visiting Uxmal, cenotes, Chichén Itzá and Valladolid. The Mitla day therefore concludes the Oaxaca segment just before the next major transfer.

This matters when choosing the entire tour. Travelers mainly interested in Oaxacan culture should assess whether enough time is allocated to workshops and archaeology. Those wishing to combine it with Mexico City and Yucatán can compare itineraries and durations in the wider [Mexico tours catalog](/mexico/tour/).

## Four stops with different experiences

**[Mitla](/mexico/place/mitla/)** is an ancient Zapotec center known for geometric stone mosaics on its buildings. It is very different from the pyramidal complexes at Monte Albán or Teotihuacan. Here the focus is on designs, stonework and the arrangement of palace courtyards.

**[Teotitlán del Valle](/mexico/place/teotitlan-del-valle/)** introduces weaving. The current excursion includes a family workshop where travelers learn about spinning, natural dyes and handmade textiles. Seeing artisans at work offers something beyond a chance to buy finished products.

**[Hierve el Agua](/mexico/place/hierve-el-agua/)** consists of natural rock formations resembling petrified waterfalls, created through mineral deposits from water. Terraces overlook a mountain valley, and the excursion description also mentions natural pools. Access to the water and precise visiting conditions depend on local rules.

The route ends with **traditional mezcal production**, made from agave. Travelers learn about the process and have a tasting. For those drawn to culture and crafts, this continues the story of the region; nature enthusiasts may find Hierve el Agua the main highlight.

| Stop | Highlight |
|---|---|
| [Mitla](/mexico/place/mitla/) | Zapotec stone patterns |
| [Teotitlán](/mexico/place/teotitlan-del-valle/) | Weaving workshop |
| [Hierve el Agua](/mexico/place/hierve-el-agua/) | Mineral cascades |
| Mezcal production | Production methods and tasting |

## Excursion terms and practical preparation

The excursion includes **shared transportation, a certified bilingual guide, admission to the archaeological site and Hierve el Agua, and a mezcal tasting**. Languages are English and Spanish. Meals, tips and personal expenses are explicitly excluded. It begins in the morning and occupies most of the day.

Wear comfortable shoes for archaeological paths and natural terraces; bring sun protection and water. Weather and temperature can change during the day at altitude and in exposed locations, so check current conditions before departure.

Respect site restrictions when visiting [Mitla](/mexico/place/mitla/). Allow sufficient time for all four stops and for the drive between them, particularly when the transfer from Oaxaca to Mérida is scheduled for the following day.

## How this day differs from other Oaxaca excursions

On the [12-day tour](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/), the preceding seventh day covers Monte Albán, alebrije-making and traditional black pottery. The Mitla day continues the craft theme but adds different archaeology, a natural landmark and mezcal. These are two distinct excursion days, and substituting one for the other would change the itinerary.

If ancient sites are your priority, choose a program with enough time for [Mitla](/mexico/place/mitla/) and Monte Albán. If you want archaeology, workshops and nature together, the Mitla day with [Hierve el Agua](/mexico/place/hierve-el-agua/) offers a broader mix. Related collections are [cultural and historical journeys through Mexico](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/mexico/) and [nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/mexico/); check each itinerary for its actual stops.

## Frequently asked questions about tours to Mitla and Hierve el Agua

### How long does the excursion last?

The stand-alone excursion description specifies **9–10 hours**. It includes an archaeological site, weaving workshop, natural attraction and tasting.

### Is lunch included?

Under the excursion's own terms, **meals are not included**. The multi-day tour's inclusions should be checked separately in its program.

### Is Hierve el Agua a real waterfall with falling water?

The famous pale cascades are **mineral formations** resembling waterfalls. There are natural pools on the terraces, but access depends on current conditions and local rules.

### On which day of Viva Mexico is Mitla visited?

**On day 8.** The journey continues toward Mérida the following day, making this one of the final stops in the Oaxaca section.

## Excursions to Monte Albán: archaeology and Oaxaca's crafts

A trip to [Monte Albán](/mexico/place/monte-alban/) suits travelers who want to discover an ancient Zapotec ceremonial center and regional crafts in one day. The archaeological complex sits on elevated ground near [Oaxaca](/mexico/place/oaxaca/). Its surviving plazas, stepped platforms and ball court are especially rewarding with a guide, who can explain the functions of the buildings and the city's development.

Ada Tours offers the [Monte Albán, Alebrijes and Black Clay Traditions excursion](/mexico/monte-alban/monte-alban-craft-villages-tour/), combining the monument with two craft communities. It suits visitors interested in both Mesoamerican history and modern artisanship.

## What the current excursion includes

The route takes **8 hours**. Pickup is scheduled **between 9:00 and 9:30**, with English- and Spanish-speaking guiding, shared transportation, admission to Monte Albán and visits to workshops. Meals, tips and personal expenses are not included.

The first section explores Monte Albán's structures. The guide explains the Zapotec people, the development of the ceremonial center and its plazas and monuments. The journey then continues to [San Antonio Arrazola](/mexico/place/san-antonio-arrazola/), where brightly painted wooden alebrije figures are made. It finishes in [San Bartolo Coyotepec](/mexico/place/san-bartolo-coyotepec/), renowned for black-clay pottery.

This is **one connected itinerary**, not three independent tours in any order. The precise time at each stop depends on the day's schedule and visiting conditions.

## Archaeology alone or a full day with workshops?

If studying the ancient city is your main goal, prioritize the time spent within the complex. Its history and major structures are described on the [Monte Albán page](/mexico/place/monte-alban/). An unhurried visit benefits from time at the main plaza, your guide's explanations and a closer look at individual reliefs.

If you are interested in links between ancient heritage and Oaxaca's modern traditions, the full eight-hour excursion offers greater variety. In Arrazola you can learn about carving and painting figures, while in San Bartolo Coyotepec you discover pottery shaping and polishing. These crafts are distinct and complement each other.

Monte Albán and Oaxaca's historic center form one UNESCO World Heritage property, but offer different experiences: the former introduces a pre-Hispanic city, the latter urban culture of later centuries.

## Preparing for the excursion

The archaeological area is open-air, with stone paving, stairs and little shade in some sections. Comfortable shoes, water, a hat and sun protection are useful. The day includes transfers between several stops, so agree on your meeting point and remember that lunch is not listed as an included service.

Mexico's INAH determines the archaeological site's opening hours and last admission. Check the current conditions and access to specific areas before traveling. The duration of the packaged excursion is not the time spent solely among the ruins.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions to Monte Albán

### Can Monte Albán be visited from Oaxaca in one day?

Yes. The current eight-hour excursion starts with archaeology and includes two craft stops. An independent visit to the complex would also require transportation.

### Are meals included?

No. Meals are not part of the [craft-villages excursion](/mexico/monte-alban/monte-alban-craft-villages-tour/). Entry to Monte Albán and visits to workshops are included.

### Is this trip worth choosing if I am interested only in ancient civilizations?

Yes, if you are willing to spend part of the day in craft villages. If you would rather study the archaeological complex in depth, first read the [site description](/mexico/place/monte-alban/) and arrange a suitable format.
